$comment: THE TWIN REGISTER — every capability whose logic has been COLLAPSED into an
@ai-matrx/* package. A local definition of one of these names in this repo is a
re-grown twin: the exact failure the client-package campaign exists to kill
(Arman: 'the logic of the packages is NEVER duplicated outside of the package').
Add a row the same session you delete a twin. Never add an allowlist entry to
silence a NEW twin — an allowlist entry is only for a definition that is
PROVABLY not the same capability, and it must say why in `reason`.

A WRAPPER is not a twin: a local function that BINDS the package function's options (unit, style, fallback) and delegates in a line or two is the sanctioned adapter, and needs no entry. A re-implemented BODY is a twin, always.

A SHAPE rule (`shapeWhy` + `shapeAllow` + `shapeCensus` on a row) catches the same capability under an UNREGISTERED name, or with no name at all. `shapeAllow` = provably NOT this capability, silent. `shapeCensus` = pre-existing bodies that ARE it and are not collapsed yet: loud every run, shrink-only, and a stale entry fails the guard.

twins.name: formatDurationMs
twins.why: THE UNIT LAW: the fleet's ~35 duration twins variously took milliseconds, seconds and minutes behind an identical `formatDuration(n)` signature, so kit ships formatDurationMs / formatDurationSeconds / formatDurationMinutes and NO bare `formatDuration`. Two host copies had already re-grown under this exact name (observational-memory format.ts, marketing crawl-session-panels.tsx) and were deleted 2026-09-07. A local `formatDuration` that BINDS unit+style+fallback and delegates is an adapter, not a twin; a local `formatDurationMs` is always a twin.
twins.shapeWhy: A millisecond count becoming a unit string is this capability whatever it is called. The name lane read GREEN on all four formatDuration* exports while aidream's dashboard carried SEVEN bodies under the private names fmtMs and fmtMsSummary, each with its own rounding, and 115 more files in this repo turned ms into `2.3s` / `1.5m` / `3m ago` inline. Pattern and its proof: scripts/duration-shape.mjs. Plain time arithmetic can never match — the rule requires a DIVISION, MODULO or THRESHOLD COMPARISON against a time base PAIRED with a duration unit label, so a timeout budget (30 * 1000), an API seconds field and a rate denominator all stay untouched. `shapeCensus` below is the pre-existing census, not an exemption: it is reported every run and is ratcheted shrink-only — a stale entry FAILS the guard.

twins.name: parseTimestamp
twins.why: The Postgres correction: a zone-less `timestamp without time zone` is UTC, not the viewer's local time — the classic 'times are off by N hours' bug. It lived in @ai-matrx/diff and in matrx-frontend's utils/datetime.ts as byte-level twins until 2026-09-07.

twins.name: formatAbsoluteDate
twins.why: Rides parseTimestamp. Collapsed 2026-09-07.

twins.name: formatFileSize
twins.why: THE byte-size formatter. It was hiding inside @ai-matrx/media's UploadProgressList React component, so six matrx-frontend twins could only reach it by depending on the media React bundle to print a byte count. Moved to kit 2026-09-07 with the display decisions written down (binary units, short labels, one decimal below ten in a unit, whole bytes below 1 KB, em-dash for unknown/negative — NEVER a confident '0 B').
twins.shapeWhy: A byte count becoming a unit string is this capability whatever it is called. The 2026-09-07 census predicted this gap ('the census method needs a shape pass') and the 2026-09-11 re-verification proved it: formatBytes, fmtBytes, humanSize, bytesHuman, formatSize, and ~60 bare inline JSX expressions that are not definitions at all and can never be caught by a name. A second review the same day proved the rule was blind to the DECIMAL (SI) family — 1000 / 1e6 / 1_000_000 — and to a GB-input body that MULTIPLIES; five live twins were returning zero findings. Both are covered now. Pattern and its proof: scripts/byte-size-shape.mjs. A capacity constant can never match: the division arms require a DIVISION or THRESHOLD COMPARISON against a byte base, and the multiply arm requires BOTH a non-literal operand (so 80 * 1024 * 1024 is out) AND the unit label on the same line outside any comment (so `limitMb * 1024 * 1024; // 25 MB` is out). Legitimate byte ceilings stay untouched.

twins.name: getInitials
twins.why: THE avatar initials formatter, duplicated between @ai-matrx/meet and @ai-matrx/messaging and in six matrx-frontend surfaces. Recorded display decision: a multi-part name takes FIRST + LAST ('Ana Maria Rivera' is AR); the six host copies printed AM.

twins.name: avatarPaletteIndex
twins.why: The deterministic avatar tint, byte-identical in @ai-matrx/meet and @ai-matrx/messaging. A random colour per render is a surprisingly loud bug, so there is exactly one hash.

twins.name: escapeHtml
twins.why: TEN copies were live across the fleet and THEY DID NOT ESCAPE THE SAME CHARACTERS — three did & < > only, two added ", four added ' (two as ', two as '), and a tenth wore the name escapeHtmlAttr while escaping only & < " into an HTML ATTRIBUTE. A string safe through one was an attribute break-out through another. kit ships ONE decided set: & < > " ' — all five, always. It is not in @ai-matrx/print because an HTML escaper must not require jspdf + html2canvas.

twins.name: ArchiveFilter
twins.why: THE ARCHIVED-ITEMS LAW's one control (Arman, 2026-09-09 — common-docs/policies/archived-items.md): the tri-state active/archived/all segmented toggle every list on the platform reveals its archive with. Shipped in design-system 0.13.0. This repo carried a local copy for part of one session — written because 0.13.0 existed unpublished and THE LATEST LAW forbids consuming an unpublished package — and deleted it the moment 0.13.0 landed. The register row is what stops the next host inventing a second answer: a boolean showArchived, a badge, or another segmented control. A behaviour the package lacks is a package change (THE SAME-SESSION LAW), never a local re-definition.
